also: near is my shirt, but nearer is my skin

terms.gloss: my tunic is nearer than my cloak: my own interest comes first
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. tunica, comparing the English “near is my shirt, but nearer is my skin”.

terms.latin: Prīma cāritās incipit ā sē ipsō.
terms.comment: We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

phrases.latin: hunc priōrem aequomst mē habēre: tunica propior palliōst
phrases.english: it’s only right that I should put him first: my shirt is nearer than my coat

phrases.latin: Meīs prius cōnsulam; tunica propior palliō est.
phrases.english: I’ll see to my own first; charity begins at home.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
